title: What Was Left Behind
logline: Weeks after a grandfather's funeral, his family finally opens the room he never let anyone into, and has to decide what a half-finished life becomes now.
human_question: When someone dies mid-task, who finishes what they started, and who decides what is let go?

premise.story: An extended family gathers to clear a deceased elder's room and settle his unfinished matters: letters, debts, a house extension left half built, a tool mid-repair. They quietly decide, out loud, what to keep, finish, or let go.
premise.place: A family home in a Kandy-district hill village, the kind with a room nobody has touched since the funeral.
premise.experience: Cupboards opening onto a life in the middle of things, and a family deciding together what happens next to what is left.

concept_links.why: The source divides what a person does into what ripens in this life, in the next, much later, or never, and gives the image of grain kept past its season that will not sprout [C057-P:L87]. A family sorting an unfinished life gives that idea an entirely ordinary, unstaged form.

Both sources insist nothing physical or mental travels on from one existence to the next [C061-P:L85; C061-M:L15]. The film can hold that teaching next to a family's instinct to keep an object 'because it was his', without resolving the tension.

what_camera_could_observe: Relatives arriving with keys, drawers and boxes opened one by one
An old ledger, notebook or letters
A half-built house extension or an unfinished repair
A family debate, conducted in the room itself, over what to keep, finish, sell or discard
One object set aside and carried out of the house
what_must_be_real: A family that has genuinely lost someone and is doing this sorting for their own reasons, in their own time, not for the camera. No possession is assigned a meaning it does not have.

possible_arc.opening: An unopened room, a bunch of keys.
possible_arc.turn: An unfinished thing surfaces, a debt, a letter, a repair, that the family must decide about.
possible_arc.ending_open: One object leaves the house in someone's hands. Where it goes next is not decided by the film.

position_hint: opening candidate: a real moment where an object belonging to someone gone could plausibly become Object 8, if a willing family allows it; the film also stands on its own as an early piece on what an ending leaves unfinished

requirements: A household that has recently lost an elder and is willing to be filmed sorting belongings
A room or set of rooms not yet cleared since a death
Enough trust for the family to speak plainly about any disagreements

suggestions.name: A hill-country village in the Kandy or Matale district
suggestions.why: A common house form with an elder's room set apart; suggested for texture and access, not for a specific household.
suggestions.verify: No specific household identified; region-level suggestion only.

risks: Turning private disagreements about inheritance into drama
Implying any object was 'meant' to be found
drop_if: No family will let the camera into this private a process
The sorting becomes staged or re-enacted for filming

connections.note: Both follow an object surviving the person who used it, one just after a death, one years later in a craftsman's hands.
A second, different real moment where Object 8 could be acquired, this time through ritual rather than sorting belongings.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
